# matmul_cpp

Performance (C++) · cpp · problem `matmul_f32` · [all examples](../examples.md)

## The problem

Make the C++ function matmul(n, A, B, C) (single precision, row-major, C = A*B) as FAST as possible on this machine (Apple Silicon, 10 cores, ARM NEON available via <arm_neon.h>). It must stay correct for every n from 1 to 2048, including sizes that are not multiples of any block size, and must write every element of C.

- **Score:** score = GFLOPS at n = 1024 (best of 3 runs). Correctness is checked first on n = 1, 7, 64, 131, 257; any wrong result makes the program invalid.
- **Files:** `examples/matmul_cpp/omega.toml`, the program `matmul.cpp`, evaluator stages: check, bench (timed alone); new bests are re-measured

Run it with:

```bash
python3 -m omega_transform run examples/matmul_cpp --minutes 15
```

## The starting program

The model may change only the code between the `OMEGA-BLOCK` markers.

```cpp
// Copyright (c) 2026 by C. Klukas
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Single-precision square matrix multiply C = A * B (row-major, n x n).
//
// This file is compiled on its own and linked with harness.cpp, which times
// matmul (wall-clock) and checks the result against a double-precision
// reference. Only the OMEGA-BLOCK region evolves; it may define only matmul as
// a global symbol (helpers must be static or in an anonymous namespace).
#include <algorithm>
#include <chrono>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>
#include <thread>
#include <vector>
#if defined(__ARM_NEON)
#include <arm_neon.h>
#endif

// OMEGA-BLOCK-START
// Computes C = A * B. C is NOT zeroed by the caller. Any number of threads may be
// used (std::thread is available); n is any size from 1 to 2048.
extern "C" void matmul(int n, const float* A, const float* B, float* C) {
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i)
        for (int j = 0; j < n; ++j) {
            float s = 0.0f;
            for (int k = 0; k < n; ++k) s += A[i * n + k] * B[k * n + j];
            C[i * n + j] = s;
        }
}
// OMEGA-BLOCK-END
```

## Benchmark results

The best result so far comes from **qwen3:30b-a3b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M (no-think)**, run locally with Ollama on 2026-10-15: a score of **167.9280** (×102.91 the starting program's 1.63177), reached after 15.16 of 15 minutes with 48 model requests.

### How it got there

The best program's ancestry, from the starting program on. "Edit" and "rewrite" are the model's changes; a parameter sweep is the engine trying values for the constants the model exposed.

| Step | Minute | Score | Kind | Idea |
|--:|--:|--:|---|---|
| 0 | 0.0 | 1.63177 | start | initial program |
| 1 | 6.5 | compile error | edit | Reorder loops to i-k-j for better streaming of B and C, enable NEON vectorization with fma intrinsics, apply cache blocking with tunable tile size to improve spatial locality, and use multithreading over row blocks to exploit all 10 cores, with parameters … |
| 2 | 10.8 | 3.60979 | fix-up | Fix the lambda capture syntax by using `&` for all captured variables to avoid the compile error, ensuring correct thread-safe access to shared data while preserving the multithreaded tiling and loop reordering strategy. |
| 3 | 12.3 | invalid | edit | Reorder loops to i-k-j to enable better streaming of B and C, reduce cache misses, and improve NEON vectorization potential, which should significantly increase performance on Apple Silicon. |
| 4 | 15.2 | 167.9280 | edit | Fix the incorrect accumulation in the inner loop by initializing C to zero before the k-loop, as the current code assumes C is already zeroed but the harness does not guarantee this, leading to wrong results for n=1. |

### The best program

What changed compared with the starting program:

```diff
--- initial
+++ best
@@ -22,11 +22,30 @@
 // Computes C = A * B. C is NOT zeroed by the caller. Any number of threads may be
 // used (std::thread is available); n is any size from 1 to 2048.
 extern "C" void matmul(int n, const float* A, const float* B, float* C) {
-    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i)
-        for (int j = 0; j < n; ++j) {
-            float s = 0.0f;
-            for (int k = 0; k < n; ++k) s += A[i * n + k] * B[k * n + j];
-            C[i * n + j] = s;
-        }
+    constexpr int TILE = 64;
+    constexpr int NUM_THREADS = 10;
+
+    const int num_tiles = (n + TILE - 1) / TILE;
+    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
+
+    for (int i0 = 0; i0 < n; i0 += TILE) {
+        int i1 = std::min(i0 + TILE, n);
+        threads.emplace_back([&A, &B, &C, n, i0, i1]() {
+            // Process tile of C rows [i0, i1)
+            for (int i = i0; i < i1; ++i) {
+                for (int j = 0; j < n; ++j) {
+                    C[i * n + j] = 0.0f; // Initialize C[i][j] to zero before accumulation
+                }
+                for (int k = 0; k < n; ++k) {
+                    float a = A[i * n + k];
+                    for (int j = 0; j < n; ++j) {
+                        C[i * n + j] += a * B[k * n + j];
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+        });
+    }
+
+    for (auto& t : threads) t.join();
 }
 // OMEGA-BLOCK-END
```
